State Vs. Umar Zahid FIR No. : 00168/2020 PS Hauz Khas  U/s 411 IPC Page no.1 of 7  Brief facts of the present case 1.

The case of the prosecution is that on 17.07.2020 at about 07.30 pm at BRT road, Ambedkar Nagar accused was found in possession of mobile phone of make Vivo Y53 belonging to complainant Kiran Devi which was stolen on 17.01.2020 at about 12.30-01.30 pm at AIIMS hospital New Delhi and which accused had retained or received knowing or having the reasons to believe the same to be stolen property and thereby committed the offence.
After completing the investigation, charge-sheet was filed against accused.
Cognizance of the same was taken.

After compliance of Section 207 Cr.P.C., vide order dated 26.08.2023 charge was framed against accused Umar Zahid for the offence u/s 411 IPC to which the accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
Prosecution Evidence 3.
In support of its case, the prosecution had examined 2 witnesses i.e. PW1 ASI Brahma Nand and PW2 SI Sanjay Singh.
The other witnesses being merely formal in nature were not summoned and PE was accordingly closed.

Reliance can be placed on judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in case titled Satish Mehra vs. Delhi Administration & Anrs. reported as 1996 JCC 507, that "in case where there is no prospect of the case ending in conviction, the valuable time of the Court should not be wasted for holding a trial only for the purpose of formally completing the procedure to pronounce State Vs. Umar Zahid FIR No. : 00168/2020 PS Hauz Khas U/s 411 IPC Page no.2 of 7 the conclusion on the future date".

On 31.07.2020 the phone was released on superdari panchnama Ex.PW1/A.
After conclusion of investigation, he filed the charge-sheet in the present case.
He had deposited the mobile phone in the malkhana after seizing the same vide seizure memo Ex.PW1/B.

Witness had correctly identified photographs of the mobile phone vide Ex.P1.

and these two persons may be apprehended if a raid is conducted.

After discussing the facts with senior officials and I/C Special staff, a raiding team consisting of SI Surender, Ct.

Before their departure, a DD no. 10 Special Staff South District dt. 17.07.2020 was made which is Ex.PW2/A.
He alongwith the team went to Pushpa Bhawan red light, secret informer pointed at accused who came there after they waited there for a while at around 07.30 pm.

Personal search of State Vs. Umar Zahid FIR No. : 00168/2020 PS Hauz Khas U/s 411 IPC Page no.3 of 7 accused was made out after disclosing him their identity and I-cards and also discussed the reason of suspicion over him.

A glass piece dummy was also recovered from his pocket which was in one black color cover.

The IMEI numbers of said mobiles were checked and were found stolen.

9. For proving the charge under Section 411 IPC, prosecution has to prove that the stolen mobile phone was recovered from the possession of accused and he knowingly/dishonestly retained or received stolen property in question, belonging to complainant.

10. It is the case of prosecution that on 17.07.2020 at about 07.30 pm at BRT road, Ambedkar Nagar accused was found in possession of mobile phone of make Vivo Y53 belonging to complainant Kiran Devi which was stolen on 17.01.2020 at about 12.30-01.30 pm at AIIMS hospital New Delhi and which accused had retained or received knowing or having the reasons to believe the same to be stolen property and thereby committed the offence.
It is pertinent to mention that in the present case the complainant Kiran Devi is not examined.
Since her presence could not be secured after issuing several process through IO/SHO/DCP concerned, then vide order dated 14.05.2024 she was dropped from the list of witnesses in the present case.
Since the complainant is not examined in the case, it could not be proved in the case that the said mobile phone of make Vivo was stolen from the complainant.
In the absence of her testimony it could also not been proved that case property belonged to her.
Further there is no other witness available on record who had witnessed the incident.
Thus, the eye account of incident is also not available.

Since the State Vs. Umar Zahid FIR No. : 00168/2020 PS Hauz Khas U/s 411 IPC Page no.5 of 7 complainant is not examined in the case, it could not be proved in the case that the mobile seized from accused was stolen one.

sentences.text: Even assuming that accused was found to be in possession of stolen mobile, but there is nothing on record to show that it was he who stole the said mobile or had received from any person with knowledge that the said mobile was stolen one.
Perusal of seizure memo which is Ex.PW2/B reveals that there was no independent witness at the time of recovery or arrest and no public witness was made to join the investigation.
At this stage, I find it pertinent to refer to the importance of joining a public witness to the investigation.
If a public witness is not available, then the prosecution must show that sincere effort was made to ensure the presence of public witness to join the raiding party.

Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Pawan Kumar vs. Delhi Administration 1987 SCC OnLine Del 290 observed:
"....Here is a case where no effort was made to join any public witness even though number of them were present.

entities.text: Pawan Kumar vs. Delhi Administration 1987 SCC OnLine Del 290
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
No plausible explanation from the side of the State vs Umar Zahid on 30 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150305142/
3 prosecution is forthcoming for not joining the independent witnesses in a case of a serious nature like the present one.

It may be that there is an apathy on the part of the general public to associate themselves with the Police raids or the recoveries but that apart, at least the I.O. should have made an earnest effort to join the independent witnesses.
No attempt in this direction appears to have been made and this, by itself, is a circumstance throwing doubt on the arrest or the recovery of the knife from the person of the accused...."

Failure to join any public person during the recovery also casts a State Vs. Umar Zahid FIR No. :
00168/2020 PS Hauz Khas U/s 411 IPC Page no.6 of 7 doubt on the story of the prosecution and strengthen the case of the accused that the case property was planted on him to falsely implicate him.
11.

The cardinal principle of criminal jurisprudence that an accused is presumed to be innocent and,
therefore, the burden lies on the prosecution to prove the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
This general burden never shifts and it always rests on the prosecution.
There is no material on record to assume that accused Umar Zahid had retained or received knowing or having reasons to believe that the said mobile phone was stolen property.
It is apparent from the above discussion that the allegations against the accused have not been proved.
Conclusion & Decision 12.
Thus, considering the entire material on record I am of the considered view that the prosecution has failed to prove its case u/s 411 IPC against the accused Umar Zahid beyond reasonable doubt.
Keeping in mind the above-mentioned discussion, accused is acquitted for the commission of the above-mentioned offence.
